selected.title: Delay to the November 2026 RTGS standards release
selected.why: Unexpected delay to the key RTGS payment system standards release.

Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Delay to the November 2026 RTGS standards release Bank of England statement Published on 27 August 2026 Statement On 27 August 2026, Swift announced its decision to delay the November 2026 Swift Standards Release based on industry’s request for additional time to prepare for the removal of the unstructured postal address format following concerns about global readiness. After careful consideration, we are also delaying what would have been the November 2026 RTGS standards release, this includes the messaging standards for CHAPS payments. Maintaining global alignment is important to preserving interoperability and to avoid the introduction of new implementation risks, and we have therefore worked closely with Swift and other major market infrastructures to support a co-ordinated approach. Our November 2026 RTGS standards release will therefore be deferred in its entirety. This is consistent with Swift delaying the entire CBPR+ standards release and avoids challenges and risks that might otherwise arise for both the Bank and industry from trying to separate changes at this late stage. We will continue to engage with Swift, other market infrastructures, and RTGS participants directly on next steps, while also providing broader updates at ISO 20022: Implementing the global payments messaging standard within CHAPS and RTGS to support organisations in amending their own planning as further detail on revised timelines becomes available. reason: Standards delay involves genuine debate about coordination costs versus implementation risk management in payments infrastructure.
angle: Delaying RTGS standards for global alignment prevents interoperability chaos, but the real cost is extended transition uncertainty harming smaller participants.
